title: Find the startup wait with strace

glossary.note: A request from a program to the operating system kernel.
The number used to identify a process.
A process handle for an open file, pipe or socket.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: On Linux, Jo's service hangs before its first log. Ren opens a terminal and asks which system call, or syscall, it waits in.

visuals.out: Fictional service: no first log line

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Build a focused trace: strace follows children with minus f, prints elapsed syscall time with minus T, and records network, read, poll and futex calls.
beats.say: Build a focused trace: strace follows children with dash F, prints elapsed system call time with dash T, and records network, read, poll and few-tex calls.

visuals.out: Run on a development process you control

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: The trace shows poll waiting on file descriptor seven. Does that prove the server is stuck in a processor loop?

visuals.out: Illustrative unfinished wait; no timing claimed

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: No. A pending poll means waiting for readiness, not burning CPU. The elapsed time appears when it returns; minus yy helps decode the descriptor.
beats.say: No. A pending poll means waiting for readiness, not burning C P U. Elapsed time appears when it returns; dash Y Y helps decode the descriptor.

visuals.text: Poll means waiting, not CPU work

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: How do I connect that descriptor to the dependency instead of guessing from one line?

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Inspect the live process's descriptor link and nearby calls. A socket suggests a network path; a futex wait points toward synchronization, but neither alone proves the root cause.

visuals.out: Replace PID with the traced process identifier

visuals.text: Map PID and FD to a resource

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Jo finds the fictional service waiting on its configured socket. After fixing that dependency, they repeat the capture and compare the call path.

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Use the trace to locate a wait, then follow its resource and surrounding calls. Tracing adds overhead, so repeat startup and treat timing as diagnostic evidence.

key_points: Follow child processes and focus the syscall filter on the suspected wait.
A blocked syscall shows waiting, not its root cause by itself.
Map the descriptor to a resource and repeat the same capture after repair.

expect.text: Poll means waiting, not CPU work
expect.note: The main syscall interpretation appears with its explanation.
